answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring each agent to stake a small, time-locked deposit at a shared vertex registry before it can trade, with the deposit slashed if peers prove duplicate identities. Reputation then accrues slowly through verified work rather than cheap signups, so a haven for honest agents emerges while sock-puppet farms stay unprofitable. A zephyr of fresh entrants still flows in, but each new identity must earn trust through attested tasks, making mass fakery expensive and easy to spot.
